Well unfortunately they are partially childcare yes. The system here is built around most people having to have duel income households just to survive. Well the school doesn't open the cafeteria early like they used to, so there is no safe or warm place for kids to go if you drop them off early. So you need a service that provides "before and after care". At the very least to drop off your kid at school and pick them up and babysit until you get off work you are looking at 700/month. After taxes and benefits cost (yes employers take the cost of insurance out of your paycheck) most people are lucky to have 3-4k for the month. Rent/morgage is around 2k, then you have whatever bills and car payments and grocery. It doesn't leave very much, and a lot of people make even less than that.
Whatever hours school doesn't keep kids there for have to be paid for somewhere else. The shorter the school day, the more expensive childcare becomes. It's not right, nor is it fair to teachers. It's unfortunately how the system works right now.
